evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: `manager_restarted` only checks that the manager PID and invocation_id are nonempty and differ. A guest reboot between the before and after snapshots can change both identifiers, falsely satisfying `manager_restarted` even though the manager restart was not observed on the same boot. The separate `boot_id_changed` check covers the intentional reboot case; requiring nonempty equal boot IDs for `manager_restarted` is a routine correctness fix in existing intended behavior.
